title: How Integrity Construction Management Fixed a 40% Cost-Type Error Rate with Agave Expense Management
summary: Integrity Construction Management fixed a 40% cost-type error rate and cut card reconciliation from a week to hours with Agave Expense Management.
body_markdown:
## About Integrity Construction Management


Founded in 2012 to provide onsite supervision and project management for development projects, Integrity Construction Management has grown into a multidisciplinary construction company based in metro-Atlanta. The firm runs two businesses side by side. Its construction management division manages horizontal work for large residential developers, from clearing and road building to onsite oversight and monthly draw packages. Its general contracting division builds the commercial pieces of those communities, such as amenity centers with clubhouses and pools, along with daycare centers, animal hospitals, warehouses, and commercial interior remodels.


Recent work includes Residences at Bridgestone, a 215-unit townhome development in Rockdale County; Residences on Kirkland, a 203-unit community built around a 7-acre lake; and Crestview, a 389-lot development in Stonecrest with over 75,000 cubic yards of blasting.


In the three years Jennifer Ellison has been Controller, Integrity Construction Management has grown from 8 employees to about 30, with crews on projects in Georgia, Tennessee, and Florida. Jennifer oversees every dollar in and out: draw packages, subcontractor payments, lien waivers, payroll, reimbursements, monthly financial reporting, and tax filings.


Residences at Bridgestone


## The Challenge: Cost Types That Wouldn't Match


Integrity Construction Management runs its accounting on Deltek ComputerEase and had previously used its native Expense Management module. Field staff would log receipts through a phone app, and charges would then post against the company's Amex. It was a real step up from the older "put your receipts on my desk" system, and Jennifer estimates it worked about 80% seamlessly.


The trouble started when Integrity Construction Management updated its project management software to Autodesk Forma Build. Agave built the Sync between Autodesk and ComputerEase, which Jennifer calls "the bridge," and it changed how the company worked. But expense coding depended on cost types matching across both systems, and that was never going to happen with the old ComputerEase Expense Management module. For example, Jennifer had defaulted fuel receipts to cost type F in ComputerEase, but some project managers set up their jobs with gas under O for other, and some used M for materials. When an expense synced to the wrong cost type, it created a brand-new budget line in the PM's budget, and reconciliation would be "chaotic."


Jennifer put the error rate at 40%. Some mornings she would open her computer to hundreds of errors, and the cleanup turned into a running argument with PMs over who had set up the job wrong. Worse, it stalled the month-end close. Credit card reconciliation is the catalyst for month-end: until cards are reconciled, PMs don't know cost to date, can't give anticipated costs, and Jennifer can't finalize budgets or monthly reports. Cards were sometimes still open on the 15th.


## Choosing Agave


Integrity Construction Management didn’t run a vendor search. Agave’s team had seen the cost-type errors firsthand while setting up the Autodesk-ComputerEase Sync and offered Integrity Construction Management the Agave Expense Management product. The leap was not small: Integrity Construction Management was leaving its native ComputerEase Expense Management system for Agave's.


What ultimately helped make the decision was Agave’s track record. Jennifer told her leadership that her experience with Agave had been great, highlighting the team’s trustworthiness, attentiveness, and ability to respond to every request during the Sync setup between Autodesk Forma Build and ComputerEase. The expectation was set: if Agave delivered on Sync, it could deliver on Expense Management.


“That level of service was the selling point, a hundred percent. They've responded to everything we've asked for in this build. I can guarantee you they're going to be just as responsive in the expense management build.”


Jennifer Ellison, CPA


Controller, Integrity Construction Management


## Implementation


Agave configured the tool around how Integrity Construction Management actually works. Employees can only code an expense to line items that already exist in the job budget in Autodesk, so the cost-type mismatch that caused errors in the old system is no longer possible. Charges flow in directly from the company Amex, and the app prompts each employee to categorize a charge once it clears, instead of waiting for a receipt to turn up.


The Agave team also came to Atlanta to onboard Integrity Construction Management’s field staff in person, fixing sign-on glitches on the spot. Construction crews are set in their ways, Jennifer notes, but once they saw how simple the app was, even the most change-resistant employees came around. Nobody pushed back on using it.


Agave Expense Management in-person implementation at the Integrity Construction Management office in Atlanta: Jennifer Ellison with Benjamin Woodman and Drew Jackson from Agave.


## The Impact


### Expense errors went to zero


Because employees can only choose budgeted line items, PMs can no longer creates stray cost lines. The 40% error rate improved to 0% within the first month.


“Setting up those safeguards has reduced my error rate down to zero. They can't choose something without a budget assigned to it and create a line item, which is what was happening in the past.”


Jennifer Ellison, CPA


Controller, Integrity Construction Management


### Reconciliation dropped from a week to a few hours


Integrity Construction Management’s 30 employees generate roughly 500 card transactions a month, which results in a 50-page Amex statement. Jennifer’s admin used to reconcile it line by line against the old system, a process that took an entire week every month. With Agave pulling charges straight from Amex and matching them to what employees enter, the same job now takes a few hours. Follow-up is easier, too: instead of asking someone to dig through a truck console for missing receipts, the app shows them the one or two charges they skipped.


### A faster month-end close


The statement drops on the 28th. By the 30th, everything is in; by the 1st, Jennifer can get numbers to the PMs; and by the 5th, they are turning in anticipated costs. Closing the month before the 15th is now attainable, whereas before, the cards alone could run past that date.


### A tool that keeps improving


Agave added reminder notifications and reimbursable expenses within weeks of Integrity Construction Management asking. This matters because many municipalities don’t take Amex, so employees have to pay with their own Visa or Mastercard.


“I was a little hesitant at first because we've all had bad experiences with tech that doesn't go as smoothly as this has. But Agave has been hand in hand with us through the whole process, allowing us to be very involved and explain exactly what we need it to do. They're just so adaptable, and that's been phenomenal.”


Jennifer Ellison, CPA


Controller, Integrity Construction Management


## Looking Ahead


Integrity Construction Management is staffed for its current volume but has growth goals, and picking up work in North Carolina or Alabama would mean more traveling supers and more cards to reconcile. With Agave, the Expense Management process now scales. Jennifer has become a strong advocate for Agave, recommending it in ComputerEase user group.


“It's a fabulous time-saving tool that allows my programs to talk to each other and save us time and headaches.”


Jennifer Ellison, CPA


Controller, Integrity Construction Management
